# Grid convergence of the free-surface pressure closure

*TensorSPH, verification record. Generated by `benchmarks/laplace_pressure_closure/make_closure_grid_doc.py` from `raw/closure_grid.json`, `raw/relax_ladder.json` and `report_force_balance.json` -- do not edit by hand.*

## 1. Case and problem

A 2-D drop of radius `R` held together by the CSF surface-tension model has to carry the
Young-Laplace jump `\Delta p = \sigma/R = 360 Pa`.

| parameter | value |
|---|---|
| radius `R` | 20.0 mm |
| surface tension `\sigma` | 7.2 N/m (10x water, shortens the capillary time) |
| density `rho0` | 1000 kg/m^3 |
| Tait exponent `\gamma` | 7 |
| capillary time `t_sigma` | 0.0333 s |
| analytic `\Delta p` | **360 Pa** |
| resolutions | `dx` = 2.0 mm (N = 362), 1.5 mm (N = 642) |
| integration window | 1.5 `t_sigma` (2000-step cap) |

`docs/verification_laplace_pressure_closure.md` implemented the Adami / Ihmsen / Adams
(2012, sec. 3.3) pressure closure and measured it **at a single resolution**
(`dx = 2.0 mm`, `c0 = 20 m/s`). It left two loose ends that this record closes:

* the best variant (`donors = interior`, 2 layers) read `+8.8 %` on the tail average but
  a different number on the final snapshot, so the reading is window-sensitive;
* the spurious current, `v_max / v_ref = 0.388`, is 3.9x Adami's own criterion (< 0.1),
  so the closure is not obviously healthy and its gain needs a resolution check.

A one-resolution reading cannot separate a discretisation error (shrinks with `dx`) from
a fixed offset. The grid below separates them.

Context from the force-side diagnostic (`report_force_balance.json`, no time
stepping): the discrete CSF force at `dx` = 2.0 mm
holds `-int rho a_r dr` = 359.1 Pa = 99.7 % of `\sigma/R` (360 Pa),
i.e. the *force* is not the limiter; whatever is left is on the pressure side,
which is what the closure touches.

## 2. What was run

`benchmarks/laplace_pressure_closure/closure_grid.py` drives `benchmarks/laplace_pressure_floor/run.py::relax()`:
calibrated-mass hex lattice (`m -> m/(1+b)`, `b = 5.9e-3`), consistent CSF with
`fit_quadratic` curvature, zero gravity, viscosity 0.01 m^2/s, `c0` = 20 m/s
(plus a 10 m/s probe), `dt` from the acoustic Courant limit rescaled to the window.

Readings, all from the same run:

| symbol | definition |
|---|---|
| `p_core` | mean pressure over `r < 0.5 R`; Tait is normalised at `rho0`, so in vacuum `p_core` *is* `\Delta p` |
| tail | mean over the last 40 % of the window (the breathing mode averages out) |
| final | the last snapshot only (window-sensitive, kept for continuity with the previous record) |
| `v_max/v_ref` | max particle speed over `sqrt(sigma/(rho0 R))`; Adami's criterion is < 0.1 |

## 3. Results

### 3.1 Every case

| case | `dx` [mm] | `c0` [m/s] | N | steps | closure | tail `\Delta p` [Pa] | tail err [%] | final err [%] | `v_max/v_ref` | compress. achieved/required |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| dx = 2.0 mm, closure off | 2.0 | 20 | 362 | 1283 | off | 223.6 | -37.9 | -42.1 | 0.030 | 0.57 |
| dx = 2.0 mm, closure on (interior, 2 layers) | 2.0 | 20 | 362 | 1283 | on | 391.8 | +8.8 | +142.8 | 0.388 | 2.41 |
| dx = 1.5 mm, closure off | 1.5 | 20 | 642 | 1710 | off | 222.9 | -38.1 | -43.6 | 0.025 | 0.56 |
| dx = 1.5 mm, closure on (interior, 2 layers) | 1.5 | 20 | 642 | 1710 | on | 347.7 | -3.4 | +6.3 | 0.090 | 1.06 |
| dx = 2.0 mm, c0 = 10 m/s, closure on | 2.0 | 10 | 362 | 642 | on | 345.5 | -4.0 | -6.7 | 0.060 | 0.93 |
| dx = 1.5 mm, c0 = 10 m/s, closure on | 1.5 | 10 | 642 | 1052 | on | 343.4 | -4.6 | -10.7 | 0.098 | 0.89 |

### 3.2 What the closure buys, at fixed resolution

| `dx` [mm] | `c0` [m/s] | tail err, closure off | tail err, closure on | gain [pt] |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2.0 | 20 | -37.9 % | +8.8 % | +29.0 |
| 1.5 | 20 | -38.1 % | -3.4 % | +34.7 |

The closure moves the reading towards `\sigma/R` at every resolution tested (largest gain +34.7 pt at `dx` = 1.5 mm). The *sign* of the residual, however, does not
survive the refinement: it is not a monotone approach to zero.

### 3.3 Does the residual shrink with `dx`?

| `dx` [mm] | closure off, tail err [%] | closure on, tail err [%] |
|---|---|---|
| 2.0 | -37.9 | +8.8 |
| 1.5 | -38.1 | -3.4 |

Refining 2.0 mm -> 1.5 mm (particles 362 -> 642) moves the
closure-off reading by -0.2 pt and the closure-on reading by -12.2 pt.

The shift is larger than the window scatter, so the residual does depend on
`dx`; with two resolutions no order of convergence can be fitted, but the
trend reported in the table is the one to carry forward.

### 3.4 Coupling with the EOS resolution floor

`c0` sets the compression `\rho/\rho0 - 1` that the Tait law needs for `\sigma/R`,
with it the pressure noise `rho0 c0^2 sigma_rho`. Lowering `c0` to 10 m/s with the
closure on:

| case | tail err [%] | `v_max/v_ref` | compress. achieved/required |
|---|---|---|---|
| dx = 2.0 mm, c0 = 10 m/s, closure on | -4.0 | 0.060 | 0.93 |
| dx = 1.5 mm, c0 = 10 m/s, closure on | -4.6 | 0.098 | 0.89 |

If the residual were only the EOS floor it would improve with `c0`; if it is the
closure operator it should not care. The table above is the measurement, not a
prediction.

## 4. Verdict against the platform criteria

| criterion | requirement | best closure-on case | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| platform, 15 % | abs err < 15 % | dx = 1.5 mm, closure on (interior, 2 layers): -3.4 % | PASS |
| paper, 3 % | abs err < 3 % | dx = 1.5 mm, closure on (interior, 2 layers): -3.4 % | FAIL |
| Adami spurious current | `v_max/v_ref` < 0.1 | dx = 1.5 mm, closure on (interior, 2 layers): 0.090 | PASS |
| closure gain (control) | closure on beats closure off | -37.9 % -> -3.4 % | PASS |

Ledger grade this record earns: **MARGINAL** (same rule as `docs/verification_ledger.md`: PASS <= 3 %, MARGINAL <= 15 %, otherwise WITHHELD).

The closure **passes the 15 % platform line** and misses the 3 % paper line, so the
residual is a residual, not a resolution of the problem. Two facts bound the claim:

* the reading is resolution dependent -- `+8.8 %` at 2.0 mm becomes -3.4 % at 1.5 mm, i.e. the sign flips, so the
  single-resolution `+8.8 %` of the previous record was not converged;
* the spurious current is too -- `v_max/v_ref` = 0.388 at 2.0 mm (> 0.1) and 0.090 at 1.5 mm.

With two resolutions no order of convergence can be fitted, so this record claims a
MARGINAL result and not a converged one; a third resolution is the next step.

## 5. Notes, traps and scope

* **Reproducibility cross-check.** The `dx` = 2.0 mm cases of this grid reproduce the
  committed single-resolution ladder of `raw/relax_ladder.json`:

  | grid case | ladder case | grid tail [%] | ladder tail [%] | diff [pt] |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `grid_dx2.0mm_off` | `closure_off` | -37.9 | -37.9 | +0.0 |
  | `grid_dx2.0mm_on` | `closure_on_interior_layers2` | +8.8 | +8.8 | +0.0 |

  Largest difference +0.00 pt, i.e. the same run to the printing
  precision (the integrator is deterministic; the pair list is rebuilt every step).

* **The final-snapshot reading must not be quoted alone.** With the closure on it reads
  far above the tail average, because the breathing mode of the drop has period ~
  `t_sigma` and a 1.5 `t_sigma` window still contains a large part of one cycle. Only the
  time-averaged readings are used for the verdict.
* **Window length.** 1.5 `t_sigma` is not equilibrium. A converged verdict needs either a
  much longer window (expensive: ~80 s per 1.5 `t_sigma` at `dx` = 2 mm on two CPU
  cores) or damping/viscosity that removes the breathing mode first.
* **Donor semantics.** Only `donors = interior` with 2 passes is on the grid; the
  `donors = all` variant of the previous record is not resolution-tested here and must
  not be assumed to behave the same.
* **Threshold.** Receivers are chosen with `rho < 0.99 rho0`; the shell width that this
  selects depends on `dx` through the kernel-support truncation, which is exactly why the
  resolution sweep is needed before the operator can be considered converged.
* **2-D only.** The cubic-spline normalisation and every number here are two-dimensional.
* **Scope.** Nothing in `src/` was changed by this record; it measures the implementation
  that `Config.surface_pressure_closure` (default `False`) already provides.

## 6. Reproduce

```
PYTHONPATH=src python benchmarks/laplace_pressure_closure/closure_grid.py
PYTHONPATH=src python benchmarks/laplace_pressure_closure/make_closure_grid_doc.py
PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/test_free_surface_pressure_closure_grid.py -q
```

Evidence: `benchmarks/laplace_pressure_closure/raw/closure_grid.json` (6 cases, 2000-step cap, `t` window 1.50 `t_sigma`)
